sermon.title: S3x in the Church part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor Kincer
sermon.summary: Love is the whole package. Paul tells believers to relax and abide where called, to stay as they are or marry without sin, to live with the time being short, and to make amends rather than sin. Jesus had brothers and sisters, and married ministers served well.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

chunks.short_answer: Stay as you are—but if you marry you have not sinned.
chunks.text:

He’s always He’s not afraid to make a judgment, is he? Hallelujah. Anyway, I suppose therefore that this is good for the present necessity or the present need, [clears the present throat] want, the present requirement that is affected by external conditions, by duty, the law of duty in regarding to one’s advantage, custom argument. It’s a very complicated word, but he’s saying the present necessity requirement that you’re in.

You see, you’re a virgin. It [clears throat] is a good for a man. What? So to be in the present condition you’re in, just what? Stay there. You may have a need, but stay there. More on his opinion. If you are bound to a wife, seek not to be loose. See, he’s saying stay in the condition you’re in. If you’re loose from a wife, seek not a wife. Relax. Don’t put pressure on you. And what are people doing in America? They’re going on to uh e-harmony.com and running to bars and all these places trying to find a man.

They’ll even go to a church because there’s a lot of men there. He says, “Relax. If you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin Mary, she has not sinned. Yet such shall have trouble in the flesh. And I want to spare you.” Why does he say if they get married they’ll have trouble in the flesh? Because if they marry the wrong person, that person is going to want them to do things against the Christian lifestyle and wanting to please them. They’re going to start compromising their lifestyle and give in to drinking, drugs, partying, barring, [clears all these throat] things that God doesn’t want us to do.

They’re a believer and their spouse is still a what? Unbeliever. And so he’s trying to explain how to approach all that. Isn’t this good? I suppose therefore that this is good because of the present distress—that it is good for a man to remain as he is: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be loosed. Are you loosed from a wife? chunks.short_answer: The time is short—live normal, use the world without abusing it.

He’s talking about the second coming. And we showed you over and over in Matthew when and Luke where Jesus said, “Always be alert and watch because you don’t know when your servant comes. Don’t live a life of drinking and partying and mistreating his people.” And so Paul is using that same mentality. See, if we’re looking for the coming of Christ, then it should affect our lifestyle is what he’s saying. So he says, because we’re looking for Christ’s coming and this world changing its fashion, he said, then those of you that have wives, live like you had none.

In other words, and [clears throat] he’s going to explain this more, live that lifestyle. Use that power of God. Use that self-control. Use that gift. [clears throat] And you know, don’t go overboard with marriage. They that weep as though they weep not. You go through difficult times, don’t make a big issue out of it. Keep a good attitude in it. You know, you’re going through unpleasant times. He said, don’t belabor it and don’t get extreme in it. You know, act like there’s no problem there. I mean, know that’s an attitude. This is good stuff, folks. I pray you get this because it can really set you free. He says, “They that rejoice as though they were rejoicing.

Everything’s going good for you. No problems or anything else.” Well, don’t get extreme in it. Just live normal. Just live like everything’s normal. He says, “They that buy as they that possess not. You got money to buy things and oh, you’re going to show off your new car to everybody and you’re going to show off your new clothes and you know this and that and your big screen TV and all the rest.” He said, “Don’t do that. Get things and act like you don’t have them.” Wow. And in other words, if you don’t have them, relax in that, too. Not having things is not the end of the world. Keep a good attitude. The guy with the big screen just has a bigger electric bill.

Are you with me? He’s saying stay moderate. Stay in the middle for the fashion of this world is passing away.

For the form of this world is passing away.

chunks.section_question: Who cares for the things of the Lord?
chunks.short_answer: The unmarried; the married care to please a spouse—marry wrong and you’ll be pulled from your Christian life.
chunks.text:
But I would [clears throat] not have you without carefulness caution. I’m going to give you some caution. All right. Now, here’s the key. He that is unmarried cares for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may what? Please the Lord. Okay. He’s using a metaphor here. He’s using an illustration that a single person isn’t distracted by a spouse to do wrong so they can focus on what? Pleasing the Lord. Now, can the married do that? Absolutely. But he’s following his his approach trying to show us and get the message across. He that is married cares for the things that are of the world. How he may what? Pleases wife. So if that wife wants to smirk marijuana, the pressure is on her to what?

Smoke marijuana. She wants to drink beer and, you know, have the guys over for Monday night football, she wants to drink beer. See, are you with me? That’s the trouble in the flesh that he wants to spare us from. He’s trying to tell us to be single is better to hang in there with the gift, with self-control until you find that person in the Lord that wants to live together, caring for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord. Are you there? Now see, my kids know if I love my wife by how I treat her they.

Know if I love Jesus by how I treat him. That’s the bottom line. If I don’t give time to Christ and show forth his character in my life, what does it tell them? I don’t love God at all. He’s just a convenient thing for me at a convenient time. Because if I really love him, I will live a life to please him. Isn’t that right? And who knows if I can save my unbelieving spouse, my unbelieving children, my unbelieving parents, my unbelieving neighbors by my what? Behavior. Say the word behavior. And remember, Paul put the behavior above the word, didn’t he?

Or Peter did. He said, “You don’t have to use a lot of words. You can win them by your behavior.”. Now, he goes on to say the same thing between a virgin and a wife. I mean, a wife and a virgin. Yeah. The unmarried woman cares for the things of the Lord to be what? Holy in body and in spirit. See, if my spirit doesn’t come out in the body, what good does that do my children? If my spirit doesn’t come out in my body, what good does that do my wife? I’m going out on her I’m down at Joe’s bar drinking with the guys. You know, I’m left her all to raise children, everything by herself and squander the money on on sport gambling and whatever. What good? So, so I come into church and and and I get in the presence of God and I feel happy, you know?

But my point is this. If we really got it in the spirit, it should come out in our lifestyle, holy, righteous. But she that is married cares for the things of the world, how she may please her husband. See, he’s back to that. If you’re in the wrong marriage, you’re going to try to please some lukewarm Christian, some unbeliever, and it’s going to cost you if you compromise their possible salvation, your kids’ possible salvation, and others because you are going to have trouble in the flesh and you don’t overcome it with self-control, gift of God, [clears it’s going to have bad results.

Throat] Is he clear? You got it. Is this good? Absolutely. I speak for your prophet, not that I may cast a snare up on you. He said, I’m not trapp trying to trap you. I’m not trying to catch you in anything and one of these gotcha things, but for that which is honorable. That you may attend on the Lord without what? Distraction. What’s his whole goal? That you serve God without being distracted by your unsaved husband, by your baby wife, by your unsaved children or rebellious children. You don’t get distracted. You keep serving God because in it, your lifestyle, your behavior can win them in the end. Now folks, I think that is just powerful stuff.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But I want you to be without care. He who is unmarried cares for the things of the Lord—how he may please the Lord. But he who is married cares about the things of the world—how he may please his wife. There is a difference between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares about the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she who is married cares about the things of the world—how she may please her husband. And this I say for your own profit, not that I may put a leash on you, but for what is proper, and that you may serve the Lord without distraction.

chunks.section_question: What if a man behaves uncomely toward his virgin?
chunks.short_answer: Make amends and get married—it’s not the end of the world; Paul gives permission, not a snare.
chunks.text:
But if any man think that he behaves himself uncommonly, disgracefully toward his virgin, now catch this. Watch this closely. Here’s a powerful Revelation. Okay, this guy is betrolled. He’s seeing a girl back there. They betrod. They, you know, they connected people to get married and they would visit each other and so forth. But he’s done something disgracefully. He’s put his hand where he shouldn’t have put his hand. They’ve done things that they maybe shouldn’t have done. Fondled. You know, [clears he said, “You’ve behaved throat] disgracefully.” Are you with me? You got that part? You should. Most of you here have gone through this stuff. All If right. scriptures.text_nkjv: But if any man thinks he is behaving improperly toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of youth, and thus it must be, let him do what he wishes. He does not sin; let them marry. Nevertheless he who stands steadfast in his heart, having no necessity, but has power over his own will, and has so determined in his heart that he will keep his virgin, does well. So then he who gives her in marriage does well, but he who does not give her in marriage does better.

chunks.short_answer: Yes—James, Joses, Judah and Simon, and sisters; married ministers were as successful as Paul.
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. See, that’s why we have such a mess in the American church today. We got too many people with their own opinions without permission. [clears But she is throat] happier if she also abides after my judgment. I think I also have the spirit of God. And uh how many agree he’s enlightening us by the spirit of God? Yes. Absolutely. Beautiful. Now in 1 Corinthians 9:5, we have no right or do we not have a right to take along a believing wife as do other apostles. The other apostles were married and when they traveled they took their wives with them.

The brothers of the Lord. Jesus had four brothers and some sisters. Unlike the Catholic Church teaches that Mary stayed a virgin all of her life. That is a very horrible lying doctor. Mary did not stay a virgin all of her life. She had sexual relationships plainly in the Bible after Jesus was born and she had children. Jesus had four brothers and sisters. And the Catholics will say, well, the word brother means relative. And it is a Jewish word for brother or relative. But what do you do about the sisters? There’s only one word for sister in the Greek here, and that’s sister. [clears throat] Okay. Mark 6:3.

Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, Joseph’s, and Judah, and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us? Also, Galatians 1:19. But other of the apostles saw I none except James, the Lord’s brother. That’s specific to James. Catholics are very wrong. And Catholics, people are very wrong for following that because then they elevate Mary up to something she is not. And then they worship her and I love my Catholic friends, but they’re totally wrong here. We should worship only Jesus. Ain’t that what it said in Revelations when he tried to worship the angel talking to him?

He said, “Don’t worship me. Worship Jesus.” Hallelujah. Adore Jesus. And so my point is this. These married ministers were just as successful as Paul. Isn’t that right? Peter, Barnabas, James, John. See, they were all married. They traveled with their wives and they were just as successful. So, what is Paul trying to teach us? He’s trying to teach us [clears throat] to hang in there in any situation we are in. There’s nothing wrong with being unmarried. You’re not a secondass citizen. There’s nothing wrong with being married. You’re not a secondass citizen.

But if you’re married to the wrong person, you’re going to have trouble in the flesh. Why? Because they’re going to try to get you to do things against your Christian lifestyle. Drink, take drugs, smoke, to smoke marijuana, smoke cigarettes, all these things that are not a good example to your children and the ones you’re living around. Isn’t that right? Sexual immorality, anger, violence. But if you’re in that kind of situation, he says, “Hang in there because you don’t know if you’re going to get them saved by your lifestyle. Hang in there if you can. You know, if they’re beating you up and and you know, there’s debauchery going on and and you’re the slave, then yeah, God’s call you to peace, you can remove yourself from that.

See, he’s trying to give us freedom to think and do what’s right. And you know, it’s not good for your kids to grow up with a dad that’s drinking and taking drugs and and doing bad things because what they see dad doing, they think is okay. So somewhere the innocent person has to be what? Protected. And who’s the innocent person in the marriage? The children. They don’t know right and wrong yet. They are counting on the parents.
